topics.title: Māui and Mahuika: The Secret of Fire
facts: Māui visits his ancestress Mahuika seeking fire.
In this telling, Mahuika gives him fire from her burning fingernails.
He repeatedly extinguishes the fire and returns asking for more.
Mahuika grows angry after she realizes she has been tricked.
Fire spreads through a forest and Māui flees.
Rain and water help end the danger in some tellings.
Fire remains in the trees used to create fire by friction.

topics.title: Rūaumoko: The Earth Beneath Our Feet

sources.title: Te Ara — Earthquakes in Māori tradition

facts: One traditional account describes Rūaumoko as a child of Ranginui and Papatūānuku.
After their separation, the children turn their grieving mother Papatūānuku over.
Rūaumoko remains with his mother beneath the earth.
He is associated with earthquakes and volcanic activity.
The trembling land is explained in this tradition through his movements.
